ORDER M.A. No.2729/2008 and M.A. No.2662/2008 These miscellaneous appeals under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are filed by the claimants Smt. Kusum Tiwari and Shri Devendra Prasad Tiwari (M.A. No.2729/2008) and Smt. Anju Mishra (M.A. No.2662/2008) being aggrieved of award dated 16.01.2008 passed by the learned Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewa (M.P.) in claim case No.91/2006 (Smt. Kusum Tiwari and another Vs. Pramod Kumar Mishra and others) on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has awarded a meager amount of Rs.1,89,500/-
in a claim case filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and has divided the total compensation in equal proportion between the parents and wife of the deceased Akhilesh Tiwari.
This division of amount of compensation is challenged by Smt. Anju Mishra, wife of the deceased besides claiming enhancement.

It is submitted by Shri Prabhat Shukla, learned counsel for the claimants that deceased Akhilesh Tiwari was the son of claimants Smt. Kusum Tiwari and Shri Devendra Prasad Tiwari and husband of Smt. Anju Mishra.

Tribunal has construed notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per annum for an accident which took place on 30.05.2006, whereas minimum wages even for an unskilled labourer on the date of the accident were to the tune of Rs.2,422/- per month.
Shri Mohd. Siddique, learned counsel for the respondent No.3-Oriental Insurance Company supports the award and submits that no indulgence is required in the matter.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, if minimum wages even for an unskilled labourer on the date of the accident i.e. Rs.2,422/- per month or Rs.29,064/- per Pramod Kuamr Mishra vs Smt.Kusum Tiwari on 4 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26617440/
3 annum is taken into consideration then, after deducting 1/3rd towards living expenses of the deceased, net dependency will come out to Rs.19,376/- per annum.

sentences.text: 40% is to be added towards Future Prospects and then, multiplier of 18 will be applicable, taking total pecuniary compensation to Rs.4,88,275/-.

Over and above which claimants will be entitled to a sum of Rs.70,000/- under the head of non- pecuniary compensation, taking total compensation to Rs.5,58,275/- against a sum of Rs.1,89,500/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.3,68,775/- (Rupees Three Lakhs, Sixty Eight Thousands, Seven Hundred and Seventy Five only) to which claimants will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
This additional amount will also earn interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.

It is also directed that total compensation of Rs.5,58,275/- will be divided between the parents of the deceased and wife of the deceased Akhilesh Tiwari that is parents and wife will get a sum of Rs.2,79,137.50/- each side along with accrued interest thereon.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
In above terms, these miscellaneous appeals are disposed of.
None for the appellants.

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is filed by the owner driver of the offending vehicle being aggrieved of award dated 16.01.2008 passed by the learned Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewa (M.P.) in claim case No.91/2006 (Smt.
Kusum Tiwari and another Vs. Pramod Kumar Mishra and others) on the ground that exoneration of the insurance company is uncalled for.

sentences.text: It has come on record and as discussed by the learned Tribunal in para 15 of the award that there was evidence to the effect that offending vehicle i.e. jeep was used for commercial purpose and admittedly jeep was insured as a private vehicle and not for commercial purpose, thus, there was violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy for which insurance company has been rightly exonerated.
Therefore, no indulgence in the matter of appeal filed by the owner driver can be shown in absence of any other evidence.
In view of above, this miscellaneous appeal fails and is dismissed.
